projects.name: 1.1.4.23 UNDP - Climate change mitigation and adaptation
projects.description:
Building upon Serbia’s NDC commitments, the action is advancing medium and long-term adaptation planning in the Republic of Serbia by formulation of a comperhensive National Adaptation Plan (NAP), enabling the Government of Serbia to build and strengthen capacities for mainstreaming climate change adaptation (CCA), produce actionable climate risk and vulnerability assessments, and implement effective methods, tools and information systems to better inform decision-making on climate risks. 
The action is also addressing the main barriers to the integration of CCA into national, sectorial and local government planning and budgeting and support the formulation of financing strategies and mechanisms for the scaling up of medium- and long-term adaptation.
The Green Agenda projects contribute to the efficient, inclusive and sustainable implementation of the Green Agenda in Serbia by improving policy and base-conditions for the more efficient implementation of the Green Agenda in Serbia, supporting pilot projects within the five priority areas of the Green Agenda and promoting opportunities for future scale-up financing.
projects.outcome: Communities have increased resilience to climate induced and human-made disasters

projects.outcome: Regional and transborder cooperation, security, and trust building are enhanced

projects.name: 1.1.3.13 UNDP - Infrastructure improvements
projects.description: Strengthening resilience at both national and local for which engineering services of various specializations are required. projects.name: 1.3.4.9 UNOPS- EU Support to Local Development Programme - EU PRO Plus
projects.description:
EU PRO PLUS focuses its work on enhancing territorial development management, supporting economic growth, and improving social infrastructure and cohesion. 
Within efforts to achieve Enhanced economic growth in targeted municipalities, the Programme supports development of economic infrastructure which shall facilitate investments and enable job creation, contributes to enhanced competitiveness of businesses through activities implemented by business support organisations, and provides direct assistance to businesses and business start-ups to procure equipment and introduce services which will contribute to creation of new jobs and strengthening of value chains.
In 2023, support to 16 projects implemented by business support organisations will be concluded, while at least 100 enterprises micro and small enterprises will be supported directly through grants. Additionally, in mid-2023 the Programme will extend support to business start-ups owned by women and youth.
Equal opportunities are promoted through all activities, while support to women is stimulated through selection criteria by additional points awarded to companies owned by women or those that already employ women and have a plan to create additional jobs for them. The activities also promote corporate social responsibility as a mandatory part of direct support to enterprises. Additionally, gender mainstreaming in infrastructure will be considered to ensure that experiences of women and men, girls and boys, are an integral dimension of the planning process.
projects.outcome: Women and men have access to more decent job opportunities and fair competitive trade

projects.description:
Designed to enhance the implementation of social inclusion policies in Serbia and provide sustainable housing solutions accompanied with active inclusion measures for the most vulnerable population, such as members of the Roma communities, disadvantaged
women, in particular women victims of domestic violence, youth in/leaving care, persons with disabilities, and others who live in inadequate housing conditions. Objective is to contribute to increased social inclusion of and gender equality among the women and men, girls and boys experiencing poverty and social exclusion enabling them to live in dignity and take an active part in society.

projects.name: 1.3.1.5 UNOPS- EU Support to Local Development Programme - EU PRO+
projects.description:
EU PRO PLUS focuses its work on enhancing territorial development management, supporting economic growth, and improving social infrastructure and cohesion. 
Within efforts to Improve development planning and introduce integrated territorial investment concept, the Programme supports development of Sustainable Urban Development (SUD) and Integrated Territorial Investment (ITI) strategies using EU territorial mechanisms. The key beneficiaries are local self-governments and regional development agencies, along with institutions at institutions at local and regional levels. The Programme also supports design of the national model for integrated and sustainable territorial development at the national level, in partnership with the Ministry of European Integrations. 

In 2023, development of 12 territorial strategies is planned to be completed, and a grant scheme for implementation of projects deriving from these strategies launched. Additionally, EU PRO Plus will implement a number of capacity building activities for stakeholders at all levels. 

Equal opportunities and representation of women in activities related to capacity building are supported by inclusion elements of gender equality in the Plan for building the capacity of national institutions for the introduction of instruments of integral territorial development.

projects.name: 2.3.1.9 Joint Programme (UNHCR)  Strengthening Migration Governance and Asylum Systems in Serbia: Enhancing policies, Protecting Rights
projects.description:
The overarching goal of the project is to enhance national authorities' capacities to achieve effective and efficient migration governance and protection of rights of individuals in need of international protection, as well as other vulnerable individuals within mixed movements in Serbia.
This objective is anchored in the principles of rights-based and route-based approaches, ensuring that the most vulnerable receive the protection and assistance they need, as well as promoting regular migration pathways for safe, regular, and orderly migration. In this context, the terms ‘individuals in need of international protection’ refers to refugees or asylum seekers while ‘other vulnerable individuals’, refers to migrants in vulnerable situation, i.e. individuals who may face significant risks or vulnerabilities without necessarily seeking asylum, including victims of trafficking or unaccompanied and separated children (UASC). The long-term impact of the project is the creation of a more robust and rights-sensitive migration and asylum management systems in Serbia. This system will be better equipped to address the complexities of mixed movements, ensuring that individuals in need of protection are identified and assisted promptly, while also supporting their long-term integration into society.

projects.name: 2.3.1.8 Joint Programme (IOM) Strengthening Migration Governance and Asylum Systems in Serbia: Enhancing policies, Protecting Rights
projects.description:
The overarching goal of the project is to enhance national authorities' capacities to achieve effective and efficient migration governance and protection of rights of individuals in need of international protection, as well as other vulnerable individuals within mixed movements in Serbia.
This objective is anchored in the principles of rights-based and route-based approaches, ensuring that the most vulnerable receive the protection and assistance they need, as well as promoting regular migration pathways for safe, regular, and orderly migration. In this context, the terms ‘individuals in need of international protection’ refers to refugees or asylum seekers while ‘other vulnerable individuals’, refers to migrants in vulnerable situation, i.e. individuals who may face significant risks or vulnerabilities without necessarily seeking asylum, including victims of trafficking or unaccompanied and separated children (UASC). The long-term impact of the project is the creation of a more robust and rights-sensitive migration and asylum management systems in Serbia. This system will be better equipped to address the complexities of mixed movements, ensuring that individuals in need of protection are identified and assisted promptly, while also supporting their long-term integration into society.
